newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa improves, no decision on test.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa improves, no decision on test.

text.p: Mother Teresa's doctors said on Friday the nun had gone 24 hours without chest pains but more time was needed to ensure she could withstand a special X-ray test to see if she needs surgery for a blocked artery.

"Mother Teresa had a good night. Her congestive failure seems to be more under control and she had no chest pain for the last 24 hours," said a bulletin issued by the Birla Heart Research Centre in the eastern Indian city of Calcutta.
Clinic officials said the 86-year-old Nobel Peace Prize winner, who entered hospital on November 22 with an irregular heartbeat, chatted with one of her doctors over morning tea.
"The doctors are still evaluating her condition and have yet to take a decision when to go for angiography," A.K. Chatterjee, the Birla centre's administrator, told reporters.
The test involves an X-ray and an opaque dye injected into blood vessels to check for arterial blockage.
The Roman Catholic missionary had juice and custard for breakfast and spoke briefly to two colleagues from her Missionaries of Charity religious order.
She was admitted to the Woodlands Nursing Home in Calcutta last Friday and was moved to the Birla clinic last Tuesday for an angiography X-ray test.
Doctors say a blocked artery will have to be unblocked by a procedure called angioplasty, which involves inserting a balloon into the artery and inflating the balloon to clear it.
Doctors have twice delayed the test, originally planned for last Wednesday, because she was too weak.
They said on Thursday that although Mother Teresa remained in critical condition, her vital signs had stabilised sufficiently to make the test possible.
Chatterjee said the doctors might opt to do both procedures at the same time. "I do not rule it out," he said.
Mother Teresa, known as the Saint of the Gutters for her work with the poor, was fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989.
She has undergone coronary angiography twice -- in the United States in 1991 and at the Birla centre in 1993. Each time she also had angioplasty.
Members of the Missionaries of Charity, which has about 4,500 nuns in some 80 countries and was founded by Mother Teresa in 1949, prayed for her recovery.
"We are having prayers all over the world for her recovery," said Sister Priscilla, spokeswoman for the order devoted to the poor, destitute and dying.
